executive_summary: Monsoon-driven seasonal disease surge (Malaria, Dengue, Leptospirosis) is currently high; Malaria cases reported 111% above baseline.
Critical healthcare demand surge anticipated mid-September due to Ganesh Chaturthi festival, requiring trauma and triage pre-planning.
Current air quality is healthy (GREEN protocol) due to monsoon precipitation, with no immediate respiratory threats.

weather.description: High humidity with intermittent monsoon rainfall

emr_signals: Sustained surge in fever-related clinical presentations across PHCs

resource_recommendations: Deploy Mobile Medical Units and triage tents on major procession routes (Lalbaug, Girgaon).
Pre-position bike-ambulances at high-risk gridlock points.
Increase buffer stock of IV fluids, ORS, and gastro-meds by 40%.

pollution_risk.lag_forecast: Stable; low risk unless abrupt transition to dry, stagnant conditions occurs.
interventions: Routine surveillance of respiratory outpatient volume.

compound_risks.rationale: High hospital bed occupancy from fever cases will be compounded by festival trauma surge, risking systemic triage failure.

24h: Maintain high clinical suspicion for Malaria/Dengue for fever presentations.
Reinforce water stagnation awareness to public.
7_day: Initiate mobilization of festival triage medical teams.
Assess current stock levels of antimalarials and IV fluids.
30_day: Conduct post-immersion surge surveillance (Gastro/Trauma) starting Sept 26.
